profile.name: Golam Wasy
profile.roleLine: Backend-first, full-stack capable. Building reliable systems and tools people actually rely on.

bio.whoami: Software Engineer with a mix of research and building real things. I enjoy both sides — digging into a problem and actually shipping something. I care about getting the details right, whether that's performance, security, or a tool that just works better than before.
bio.mission: Turning complex business requirements into working software. Experienced in Java and Spring Boot on the backend, React and Angular on the frontend, with AWS, Docker, Kubernetes, and CI/CD pipelines in between.

experiences.desc: Working on the Control Tower team within a digital payments platform. Most of my work has been around an internal support app used by customer service, finance, and operations teams to handle post-sale workflows — things like invoice adjustments, payments, and audit reports. On the backend I work on a Spring Boot microservice that surfaces this data, and on the frontend, helping move parts of the app from Retool to React.
Worked on my Master's thesis, exploring how different data normalization approaches affect anomaly detection on real-world datasets.

experiences.company: University of Helsinki & Nokia Bell Labs
experiences.desc: Part of a joint research project looking at data efficiency techniques for mobile networks, mostly evaluating how normalization methods hold up on telecom data.
Built and maintained mobile apps and a web console for clients, handled the backend APIs, and worked with their database and cloud setup.
My first proper backend role — writing Spring Boot code, migrating databases, and getting familiar with deploying things on AWS.
